clue.text: Footwear that's wrecked, not aged

indicators.note: not here means the letters of the word aged are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: something wrecked deliberately has been sabotaged
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: Shoes that are smashed up but not old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AGED from SABOTAGED (wrecked), leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog worn by French peasants, a kind of shoe.

clue.text: Lunatic in the faculty? Not so

parts.note: sight or hearing is a sense, one of the body's faculties
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Is there a madman among the university staff? No.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' suggests university staff, but here it is a bodily power like hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A senseless act is foolish and crazy, without reason.

clue.text: Low character makes bishop halt

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to halt is an old word meaning to walk lame

explanation.surface: A base person causes a bishop to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was the pompous reactionary drawn by the cartoonist David Low, so 'Low' is a name, not 'base'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous cartoon creation of the artist David Low was Colonel Blimp.

clue.text: Article about East published in foreign capital

indicators.note: about here means around, so the article is wrapped round the compass point

parts.note: the definite article
a newspaper ran a story when it published it

explanation.surface: A news piece on the East appeared in an overseas city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside THE to make TEHE.
explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling names the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Equipment rigged up as a trap

indicators.note: rigged suggests something fixed or set up crookedly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Gear has been set up to form a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' rearranges UP AS A TRAP; the surface sounds like a hunter laying gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the gear or machinery needed for a task, a synonym of equipment.

clue.text: A fare on bus, for example

parts.note: board is food or meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A ticket price paid on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like the bus ticket price, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a vehicle such as a bus or ship is being on board it.

clue.text: Of necessity, noble half-heartedly leads army

indicators.note: leads puts the shortened noble in front of the army
half the heart taken out: one of the two middle letters is dropped

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman
a force is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Inevitably, an aristocrat without enthusiasm commands the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one E from the double-E centre of PEER, leaving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old adverb meaning by force of circumstance, necessarily.

clue.text: River one crosses by burning boats

definitions.text: River one crosses by burning boats

parts.words: River one crosses by burning boats
parts.note: a stream that, once crossed, commits you, just as burning your boats leaves no retreat

explanation.walkthrough: Julius Caesar crossed this river in 49 BC, committing himself to civil war; the phrase now means a point of no return.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing it is the proverbial irrevocable step, the same idea as burning one's boats.

clue.text: Job for academic, distributing this port round university

indicators.note: round places the scrambled letters around the abbreviation
distributing spreads the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Work for a scholar, handing out port around the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink passed round a college table, and 'distributing' fits that picture, but it is the anagram signal; 'round' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the post of a tutor, a teaching role in a college.

clue.text: Authority, for example, to broadcast in sound only

parts.note: say introduces an example, as in say, ten

indicators.note: in sound only says the word counts by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to sow seed is to scatter it broadly

explanation.surface: Power, for instance, to transmit only on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but it is the farmer scattering seed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final word on a matter, the power to decide, is having this.

clue.text: Keep in touch with character in soap opera

definitions.meaning: to sit right next to something, adjoining it
a resident of the Australian TV soap ..., whose cast are all people next door

explanation.surface: Stay in contact with someone who appears in a TV serial.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is a long-running Australian soap opera popular in Britain, so any of its characters is one of the title's people.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to adjoin or border on; as a noun, a person living next door, as in that soap.

clue.text: Companion for a sandwich course, some say

definitions.meaning: a mate or workmate, in dialect from the coalfields of Wales and northern England
an informal northern English word for a bread roll with filling

explanation.surface: A friend to share a work-and-study course with, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich course is a British college course alternating study with work; 'some say' flags that both senses are regional words, and the rest is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: In regional British speech the same word means a pal and a filled roll.

clue.text: Beethoven work among pieces in prom — or encore etc.

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the following words are smashed and the letters reassembled

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece by Beethoven played at the Proms, or as an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' rearranges PROM OR ENCORE ETC; 'pieces' wants to mean musical works, which suits the concert-hall surface.
explanation.definitionFit: His Piano Concerto No 5 in E flat is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Declining to rebuild Big Ben

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting the letters together in a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Refusing to reconstruct the famous London clock tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges BIG BEN. 'Declining' reads as refusing but means fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide going out is falling away, so the word means waning or getting less.

clue.text: Person who slanders scandalous knight? Right

parts.note: Sir Benjamin Backbite is a gossiping knight in Sheridan's play The School for Scandal

explanation.surface: Someone smearing a disgraceful knight? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scandalous' points to Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal, whose gossip Sir Benjamin supplies the name.
explanation.definitionFit: One who speaks maliciously about people behind their backs is a slanderer.

clue.text: A container like this gets assembled, led in plant

parts.note: a can is a tin container
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A tin made this way gets put together in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory beside 'assembled', but it is the definition: a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean herb with spiny leaves, copied in carvings on Corinthian columns.

clue.text: Female writer's needing shade below this rock

parts.note: George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A woman novelist needs a colour beneath this stone.
explanation.walkthrough: George Sand is the classic crossword female writer; in a down clue 'below' means the shade comes after her name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sedimentary stone made of compressed grains, a kind of rock.

clue.text: Special call needed for chap to enter this sort of work

indicators.note: to enter puts the man's name inside the rearranged letters
special suggests a modified or unusual arrangement of the letters

parts.note: Eric is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A particular phone call is required for a man to start office duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' gives CLAL from the four letters of the call; 'to enter' sends the chap in. 'this sort of work' points back to the clue's own picture of office duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Office work of filing and paperwork done by clerks is described this way.

clue.text: Support Liberal policy finally, as introducer of item two

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word policy

explanation.surface: Backing the final part of a Liberal Party programme.
explanation.walkthrough: A speaker opens a second point with this word.
explanation.definitionFit: This adverb is used when introducing the second point in a list.

clue.text: Simplicity of style obvious in Madonna I've tested

indicators.note: obvious in says the letters can be seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The pop singer's style is plainly unsophisticated, as I have tried out.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across madonNA I'VE TEsted.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent artlessness, as in naive painting's unschooled style.

clue.text: A form of gambling

parts.note: reads as a type of betting, but means a printed form that gamblers fill in, as on the football pools

explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British weekly betting game played by filling in slips of paper with match predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the slip filled in to bet on the pools, literally a piece of paper used for wagering.

clue.text: Concerned with light output from working coal pit

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Interested in lamps that come from an active colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges COAL PIT; 'output from' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision and to the behaviour of light.

clue.text: Not on the alert, general is captured by agent

indicators.note: is captured by puts the general inside the agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Caught napping, a general is taken by an enemy spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being drowsy, ready to doze, is the opposite of being wide awake.

clue.text: Creation of favourable image about Left in what we read

indicators.note: in places the short pieces inside the longer word

parts.note: publications are books and papers that people read
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Building a good reputation is covered in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' tempts as political, matching the image-making surface, but it is only its abbreviation; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the profession of managing how a company or person is seen by the public.

clue.text: Lofted shot caught in sort of helmet

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the helmet

parts.note: a pith helmet is a tropical sun hat
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A ball hit high is caught by someone in a sun helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pith helmet is a lightweight colonial sun hat.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a high approach shot onto the green is this.

clue.text: Confess nothing when he's left before magistrate

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: left means departed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: the letters of he, the possessive marker adding none
to be up before the magistrate is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Admit nothing when he has gone off to face the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' gives WN; 'up before the beak' is British slang for being in court, which is why 'before magistrate' supplies the final pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit a fault, an idiom for confessing.

clue.text: The Duchess of Malfi, for example

definitions.text: The Duchess of Malfi, for example

parts.words: The Duchess of Malfi, for example
parts.note: the name of Webster's Jacobean play, and also a noble rank held by its heroine

explanation.walkthrough: Both the play's name and the word Duchess itself exemplify the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A play has a name under which it is known, and a duchess holds a noble rank.

clue.text: It combines calm start with finish in tumultuous score

definitions.text: It combines calm start with finish in tumultuous score

indicators.note: start points at the first letter of the word calm
in places the synonym inside the scrambled letters
tumultuous means wildly disordered, so the letters of the word score are rearranged

parts.note: the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A musical build-up starts quietly and ends loudly in the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumultuous' makes RESCO; 'in' sets the finish inside before the last letter. The whole clue also describes the swell itself, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradual increase in loudness moves from quiet to a loud climax, as the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Drug taken before sport can produce rowdy behaviour

indicators.note: taken before puts the drug's word ahead of the sport's word

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
play means sport or fun

explanation.surface: Taking narcotics before a game leads to rough conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: It is boisterous, rough fun, the noisy kind of messing about.

clue.text: Failure, we hear, in Northern people —-or parts of race

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: the Lapps are the people of Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A breakdown is reported among Arctic folk or in stages of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or parts of race' offers a second sound-alike, LAPS, circuits of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or brief failure of concentration or standards.
